# Atlas vs manual UI — interaction map and alignment

## 1. Interaction flow overview

### A) Manual UI flow

```
User (React)
  → fetch(apiUrl("/api/..."))  [frontend/src/api/client.ts, spotify.ts]
  → FastAPI backend.product_shell (uvicorn :8787)
  → routers: transport | chat | atlas | shell | memory | spotify
  → services: transport_engine, atlas_http, normalize, product_memory_store, …
  → JSON / HTML response
  → React state (Zustand useAppStore) + local component state
  → re-render (modes, map iframe blob URL, lists, etc.)
```

**Shell commands:** The UI does **not** poll when the user only uses widgets; **`ShellCommandListener`** polls `GET /api/shell/poll` every ~600ms to apply **Atlas-issued** commands (`frontend/src/components/ShellCommandListener.tsx`).

### B) Atlas flow

```
User (voice/text in Atlas orchestrator)
  → Atlas Flask API :5055 (session, tools) — not the product FastAPI
  → tool_executor.py executes tools (web_search, memory_*, cspe_*, music, …)
  → Some tools call FastAPI:
        POST {PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/api/shell/enqueue   (UI commands)
        POST {PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/v1/search_stops|/v1/route   (graph JSON)
        browser open CSPE_FRONTEND_URL   (open map)
  → Chat in React: user types in rail → POST /api/chat → atlas_http.send_text_and_wait → Atlas /text + poll /ui
  → FastAPI normalize_atlas_ui → structured_outputs → React
  → Voice: POST /api/atlas/input-mode + GET /api/atlas/ui polling → syncAtlasVoiceUi (store) — no /chat
```

**Side by side**

| Stage | Manual UI | Atlas |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Primary HTTP to product | React → **FastAPI `/api/*`** | Atlas process → **FastAPI `/api/shell/enqueue`, `/v1/*`, optional `/api/chat` proxy** |
| “Brain” for NLU | N/A (user drives UI) | **Atlas :5055** |
| Chat transcript in UI | **`postChat` → `/api/chat`** | Same **`/api/chat`** when user sends text in rail |
| Structured content | From **`/api/chat`** response (`normalize_atlas_ui`) | Same; voice uses **`/api/atlas/ui`** + `syncAtlasVoiceUi` (does not append chat history the same way as `applyChatResponse`) |

---

## 2. Feature-by-feature comparison

| Feature | UI path (manual) | Atlas path | Same underlying logic? | Same result shape? | Same UI outcome? |
|--------|-------------------|------------|-------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| **Transport: stop search** | `GET /api/transport/stops/search` → `transport_engine.search_stops` → `search_stations_autocomplete` + station layer (`client.ts`, `transport_engine.py`) | Tool **`cspe_search_stops`** → `POST {PRODUCT_SHELL}/v1/search_stops` → `cspe_v1_graph.search_stops_v1` → **`search_stops_autocomplete`** | **No** — different `queries` helpers (station-oriented vs stop-oriented autocomplete) | **No** — UI `{matches:[...]}` vs v1 `{stops:[...], graph_mode, count}` | **No** — Atlas does not fill React search boxes; agent gets lists only |
| **Transport: route** | `POST /api/transport/route` → `compute_route` / `compute_route_stations` (rich envelope) | Tool **`cspe_route`** → `POST /v1/route` → raw **`shortest_path`** result | **Partial** — both use `shortest_path` for stops; UI can also do **station** routing | **No** — v1 returns Flask-era `{result: ...}`; UI gets `TransportRouteResponse` | **No** unless shell **`cspe_transport_route_view`** updates Zustand + user refreshes map |
| **Transport: map HTML** | `POST /api/transport/map` → `render_transport_map_html` | **No direct Atlas → map API**; optional **`cspe_open_transport_map`** (browser URL probe); or shell commands to change store + user/map refresh | **N/A** for agent-only | **N/A** | **Often divergent** — agent usually does not trigger `postTransportMap` |
| **Transport: stats** | `GET /api/transport/stats` | **No Atlas tool** for stats in registry path (not in `tool_executor` grep) | — | — | — |
| **Chat (text)** | `POST /api/chat` | User message in rail → **same `POST /api/chat`** (`AtlasRailPanel.tsx`, `chat.py`) | **Yes** (same FastAPI + `send_text_and_wait`) | **Yes** (`normalize_atlas_ui` → structured blocks) | **Yes** (history + structured outputs) |
| **Chat (voice)** | Hold-to-talk → `POST /api/atlas/input-mode` + poll **`GET /api/atlas/ui`** | Session lives in Atlas; UI only **mirrors** `/ui` | **Same Atlas session**, different **product** endpoints vs text chat | **`syncAtlasVoiceUi`** updates summary/images/panels **without** same chat history rules as `applyChatResponse` (`store.ts`) | **Partially aligned** — visual panels sync; **chat transcript** differs from text mode |
| **Shell: mode / nav / transport / memory project** | User uses **`ToolRail`**, router, transport controls (Zustand) | Tools **`cspe_set_mode`**, **`cspe_navigate`**, **`cspe_transport_*`**, **`cspe_memory_project`** → **`POST /api/shell/enqueue`** (`shell.py`) → **`ShellCommandListener`** | **Commands are shared** (same enqueue/poll contract); **not** same code path as clicking UI | N/A (commands) | **Yes** if commands valid — store updates match manual actions |
| **Structured outputs push** | Normally from `/api/chat` | Tool **`cspe_apply_structured_outputs`** enqueues **`apply_structured_outputs`** → `applyChatResponse` | **Same store ingest** as chat | Same `StructuredOutput[]` | **Yes** |
| **Memory (product tasks)** | Full CRUD: **`/api/memory/projects|tasks`** → SQLite `product_memory_store.py` (`MemoryMode.tsx`, `client.ts`) | **`cspe_memory_project`** only sets **`memoryProjectId`** in Zustand via shell — **no** server CRUD from Atlas | **No** — Atlas **`memory_*` tools** use **Atlas’s own SQLite** (`atlas_client/tools/memory.py`), not product DB | **No** — two memory systems | **No** — agent “memory” ≠ product task list unless explicitly bridged |
| **Spotify / music (streaming)** | **`/api/spotify/*`** only (`spotify.ts`, `MusicMode.tsx`) | **No** product Spotify tools in `tool_executor` | **No** | **No** | **No** — music UI is manual-only |
| **Music (Atlas tool)** | N/A | Tool **`music`** → **local `music_player`** (e.g. yt-dlp), not Spotify API (`tools/music.py`) | **No** | **No** | **No** — different stack from Spotify mode |
| **Visual panels / images** | From **`applyChatResponse`** / **`syncAtlasVoiceUi`** via `ingestStructuredOutputs` (`store.ts`); **`VisualBoardMode`** reads `visualPanels` | Atlas **`visual_board`**, **`image_search`**, **`web_search`** feed **`/ui`** → **`normalize_atlas_ui`** (text chat) or voice sync | **Same normalization** when content arrives as structured outputs | **`visual_board`**, **`image_results`** shapes in `normalize.py` | **Yes** when same `/ui`/`structured_outputs` path; voice omits full chat append |

## 3. Endpoint usage comparison

### Called by the frontend (React)

From `frontend/src/api/client.ts`, `spotify.ts`, `ShellCommandListener.tsx` (relative `/api` or `apiUrl`):

| Area | Endpoints |
|------|-----------|
| Atlas rail | `POST /api/atlas/input-mode`, `GET /api/atlas/ui`, `POST /api/chat` |
| Transport | `POST /api/transport/map`, `GET /api/transport/stats`, `GET /api/transport/stops/search`, `POST /api/transport/route` |
| Shell (poll only) | `GET /api/shell/poll` |
| Memory | `/api/memory/projects`, `/api/memory/tasks` (+ CRUD) |
| Spotify | `/api/spotify/login-url`, `callback`, `status`, `play`, `playlists`, `search`, … |

**Frontend does not call** `GET /health` or `POST /v1/*` (those are for Atlas tools and ops).

### Called by Atlas tools (via `tool_executor.py`)

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `POST {PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/api/shell/enqueue` | All **`cspe_*`** shell tools |
| `POST {PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/v1/search_stops`, `POST .../v1/route` | **`cspe_search_stops`**, **`cspe_route`** |
| **Not FastAPI:** Atlas **`memory_*`**, **`music`**, **`web_search`**, **`image_*`**, **`visual_board`** | Internal / external services |

### Shared (both “product” and Atlas-driven UI)

| Endpoint | Frontend | Atlas |
|----------|----------|--------|
| `/api/chat` | Yes (text) | Same |
| `/api/atlas/*` | Yes | N/A (Atlas is server) |
| `/api/shell/enqueue` | No (only **poll** reads) | Yes (Atlas writes) |
| `/api/transport/*` | Yes | **No direct** — v1 used instead for search/route tools |

### Duplicated capability (transport)

| Capability | UI | Atlas tools |
|------------|-----|-------------|
| Stop search | `/api/transport/stops/search` | `/v1/search_stops` |
| Route | `/api/transport/route` | `/v1/route` |

**Mismatch:** Two pipelines (`search_stations_autocomplete` + rich route **vs** `search_stops_autocomplete` + raw `shortest_path`), intentionally preserved when Flask was merged.

---

## 4. Logic duplication vs shared logic

| Area | Shared? | Notes |
|------|---------|--------|
| **Graph bundle** | **Yes** | `transport_engine.get_bundle()` and `cspe_v1_graph` both use same bundle load path |
| **Stop search (UI vs v1)** | **No** | Different `src.core.queries` functions |
| **Route (UI vs v1)** | **Partial** | Same `shortest_path` core; UI adds station path, errors, etc. |
| **Atlas `/ui` → React** | **Yes** | `normalize_atlas_ui` (`normalize.py`) for `/api/chat`; voice uses raw `structured_outputs` from `fetchAtlasUi` |
| **Shell commands** | **Yes** | Single queue in `shell.py`; **`ShellCommandListener`** is the only consumer |
| **Product memory** | **UI only** | Atlas **`memory_*`** is separate datastore |
| **Spotify** | **UI only** | No Atlas tool → FastAPI Spotify |

---

## 5. Result and rendering differences

| Feature | Data model alignment | Update mechanism | Display inconsistency risk |
|---------|----------------------|------------------|----------------------------|
| **Chat (text)** | Structured blocks from `normalize_atlas_ui` | `applyChatResponse` | Low |
| **Chat (voice)** | Same `StructuredOutput` shape from `/api/atlas/ui` | `syncAtlasVoiceUi` — **does not push assistant text into `chatHistory`** the same way (`store.ts` 145–153 vs 115–131) | **High** — rail shows voice lines separately in component state vs store history |
| **Transport** | UI uses REST responses; Atlas uses v1 JSON or shell | Shell can set paths; **map refresh** is still driven by **`TransportMode`** `refreshMap` when state changes | **High** — agent can set store without recomputing map if effects don’t run as for manual |
| **Visual** | `visual_board` / images in structured outputs | Store | Medium — voice vs text path |
| **Product memory** | DTOs from `/api/memory/*` | Local fetch | N/A for Atlas |
| **Spotify** | Spotify Web API via FastAPI | N/A | N/A |

---

## 6. Command vs data model

| | **UI (data-driven)** | **Atlas (tool-driven)** |
|--|----------------------|-------------------------|
| **Typical pattern** | `fetch` → JSON/HTML → **setState** / Zustand | Tool **receipt** in Atlas + optional **HTTP side effects** |
| **Transport** | Direct **`/api/transport/*`** | **`/v1/*`** for raw graph ops; **shell** for mirroring UI state |
| **“Same screen” updates** | Immediate from response | **`/api/shell/enqueue`** → poll → **`applyOne`** — **command queue**, eventual consistency (~600ms) |
| **When Atlas returns data to React** | Via **`/api/chat`** / **`/api/atlas/ui`** as **structured_outputs** | Same + **`cspe_apply_structured_outputs`** command |
| **When Atlas sends commands** | **`cspe_set_mode`**, **`cspe_transport_*`**, etc. | Always **enqueue**, not returned as chat body |

**Interpretation:** The product shell is **dual**: **REST** for human-driven CRUD and map, and a **command channel** so the agent can drive the **same Zustand fields** as clicks — but graph **search/route** for the agent still uses **`/v1`** while the UI uses **`/api/transport/*`**.

---

## 7. Architectural inconsistencies

1. **Two transport search/route semantics** (UI `/api/transport/*` vs Atlas `/v1/*`) — drift risk for “same” feature.  
2. **Two memory systems** — Atlas **`memory_*`** vs product **`/api/memory/*`**.  
3. **Two music systems** — Spotify (FastAPI + React) vs Atlas **`music`** (local player).  
4. **Voice vs text chat** — different store updates (`syncAtlasVoiceUi` vs `applyChatResponse`).  
5. **Shell queue** — good unification mechanism, but **transport map** is not automatically refreshed from every shell command.  
6. **No Atlas → Spotify** — agent cannot drive the same music surface as the user without new tools.

---

## 8. Unification opportunities (concrete)

| Goal | Suggestion |
|------|------------|
| **Single transport search/route semantics** | Either: (a) implement Atlas tools on top of **`/api/transport/stops/search`** + **`/api/transport/route`** with an adapter in `tool_executor`, or (b) deprecate `/v1` and align **`v1`** implementation to call the **same service functions** as `transport_engine` (one canonical implementation). |
| **Canonical endpoints** | **`/api/transport/*`** for interactive product; **`/v1/*`** only as thin compatibility or removed once Atlas uses `/api`. |
| **Shell + data** | Keep **enqueue** for UI mirroring; add **explicit** “refresh map” command or **server-side** map push if full parity is required. |
| **Memory** | Choose: (a) migrate Atlas **`memory_*`** to product SQLite via new tools, or (b) rename UI “Memory” vs Atlas “Notes” to reflect two domains. |
| **Music** | Add **`spotify_*` tools** proxying FastAPI if agent should control Spotify; or document that **Spotify = UI only**, **Atlas music = local player**. |
| **Voice/text** | Unify **`syncAtlasVoiceUi`** with **`applyChatResponse`** rules for history/panels or document intentional difference. |

---

## 9. Clean target model (conceptual, no code change)

- **One FastAPI process** as **authoritative** for: transport (one implementation), Spotify, product memory, shell queue, Atlas HTTP proxy (`/api/chat`, `/api/atlas/*`).  
- **Atlas** = **alternative input modality** (NLU + tools); tools should call **canonical FastAPI actions** where possible, not parallel `/v1` semantics unless strictly needed.  
- **React** = **renderer + local state**; **shell commands** = **declarative UI deltas** (mode, paths, transport state, structured output injection).  
- **Ideal:** every **feature** maps to **one backend action** (function or use-case), invoked by **UI REST** and/or **Atlas tool adapter**, with **one** structured result model for display.

---

## Short verdict

- **Aligned:** Text chat via **`/api/chat`**, **`normalize_atlas_ui`**, shell **enqueue/poll** for mode/navigation/transport view/memory project/structured outputs.  
- **Partially aligned:** Voice UI sync; transport (UI **`/api`** vs Atlas **`/v1`** + shell).

# Music unification — architecture analysis and migration plan

## 1. Current music architecture overview

### A) UI / Spotify path (canonical product music)

**Flow**

```
User → React MusicMode → frontend/src/api/spotify.ts
  → FastAPI backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py (prefix /api)
  → Spotify Web API (accounts.spotify.com + api.spotify.com)
  → User’s active Spotify Connect device / Spotify app plays audio
```

**Behavior**

- **Auth:** OAuth Authorization Code; tokens stored under `data/spotify_tokens.json` (and in-memory `_store`), loaded on API start (`spotify.py`: `_token_path`, `_load_store_from_disk`, `_persist_store_unlocked`).
- **Config env (representative):** `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI` (default `http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback`), optional `SPOTIFY_TOKEN_PATH` (`spotify.py` ~48–52, ~110–120).
- **Playback:** `PUT /v1/me/player/play`, `PUT /pause`, `POST /next`, `GET /me/player`, `GET /search`, playlists, saved tracks, etc. — all via **`requests`** from FastAPI to Spotify (`spotify.py` ~641+).

**Key frontend**

- `frontend/src/modes/MusicMode.tsx` — connect, playlists, search, play, pause, next, polling status.
- `frontend/src/api/spotify.ts` — wraps `/api/spotify/*`.
- `frontend/src/pages/SpotifyCallbackPage.tsx` (OAuth callback; implied by imports/routes in prior context).

**Key backend**

- `backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py` — single router for all Spotify endpoints.
- `backend/product_shell/main.py` — `include_router(spotify.router, prefix="/api")`.

**External APIs**

- Spotify OAuth + **Spotify Web API** only (no local audio engine for playback).

---

### B) Atlas / local-player path (legacy parallel system)

**Flow**

```
User speaks to Atlas → tool "music" → src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tool_executor.py (elif name == "music")
  → src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/tools/music.py → execute_music_action
  → src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/audio/music_player.py
  → YouTube Data API v3 (search) + yt_dlp (stream URL) + python-vlc (local playback on Atlas host)
```

**Behavior**

- **No FastAPI.** No Spotify. No shared token with the UI.
- **`music_player.py`:** `_search_youtube` → `_extract_stream` with **yt_dlp** → **VLC** `MediaPlayer` plays stream on the machine running the Atlas process (`music_player.py` entire file; **hardcoded default `YOUTUBE_API_KEY`** at line 12 — operational/security risk).
- **Tool contract:** `action` ∈ `play|pause|resume|stop`, optional `song` query for play (`tools/music.py`, `tools_registry.json` ~113–145).
- **Registry:** `dependencies": ["vlc", "yt_dlp"]` — documents the stack, not CSPE root `requirements.txt` (those packages are **not** listed there; they are effectively **Atlas-runtime** deps).

**Where it runs**

- Same host as Atlas (wake/API process). Audio comes out of **that** machine’s VLC, not the user’s Spotify Connect target.

---

### Side-by-side

| Aspect | UI / Spotify | Atlas / local player |
|--------|----------------|----------------------|
| **Entry** | `MusicMode` + `spotify.ts` | Tool `music` → `execute_music_action` |
| **Backend** | FastAPI `spotify.py` | None (in-process Python) |
| **Playback engine** | Spotify Web API → Connect device | VLC + YouTube stream |
| **Search** | `GET /api/spotify/search` → Spotify catalog | YouTube Data API in `music_player._search_youtube` |
| **Auth** | OAuth to Spotify | YouTube API key env (with insecure default in code) |

---

## 2. Feature comparison

| Music capability | UI / Spotify path | Atlas `music` path | Same system? | Same result? | Notes |
|------------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------|--------------|--------|
| **Search** | Spotify track search (`/api/spotify/search`) | YouTube search for first video | **No** | **No** | Different catalogs and IDs |
| **Play track** | URIs / context_uri → Web API `play` | `play_song(query)` → YT + VLC | **No** | **No** | Spotify vs local stream |
| **Pause / resume** | `/api/spotify/pause` + implicit resume via `play` | VLC `pause` / `play` on local player | **No** | **No** | Different APIs |
| **Next track** | `/api/spotify/next` | **Not exposed** in `music` tool | **No** | **No** | Atlas tool has no `next` |
| **Playlist access** | `/api/spotify/playlists`, tracks, saved | **None** | **No** | **No** | — |
| **Playback device** | User’s **Spotify Connect** device | **Local VLC** on Atlas host | **No** | **No** | Core UX difference |
| **Authentication** | Spotify OAuth (+ token file via FastAPI) | YouTube API key in `music_player` | **No** | **No** | — |
| **State / status** | `GET /api/spotify/playback`, `status` | No integration with UI; local prints/logs | **No** | **No** | React does not see Atlas VLC state |
| **UI update** | React state + polling `playback` / `status` | No product-shell integration | **No** | **No** | Shell has no `music_*` command types |

---

## 3. Code and endpoint inventory

### UI / Spotify

| Kind | Path |
|------|------|
| **Frontend** | `frontend/src/modes/MusicMode.tsx`, `frontend/src/api/spotify.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/music.css`, `SpotifyCallbackPage.tsx` (OAuth) |
| **FastAPI** | `backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py` |
| **Mounted** | `/api` + routes below |

**FastAPI Spotify routes (from grep)**

- `GET /api/spotify/login-url`, `POST /api/spotify/callback`, `GET /api/spotify/status`, `GET /api/spotify/probe`, `POST /api/spotify/disconnect`
- `GET /api/spotify/playlists`, `GET /api/spotify/playlists/{playlist_id}/tracks`
- `GET /api/spotify/saved-tracks/summary`, `GET /api/spotify/saved-tracks`
- `POST /api/spotify/play`, `GET /api/spotify/search`, `GET /api/spotify/playback`
- `POST /api/spotify/pause`, `POST /api/spotify/next`

**Env / config**

- `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI`, `SPOTIFY_TOKEN_PATH`, `SPOTIFY_OAUTH_SHOW_DIALOG` (see `spotify.py` router), plus Vite `VITE_*` for API base as elsewhere.

---

### Atlas `music` (local)

| Kind | Path |
|------|------|
| **Tool definition** | `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tools_registry.json` — tool `"music"` (~113–145) |
| **Executor** | `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tool_executor.py` — `elif name == "music"` (~282–294) |
| **Tool logic** | `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/tools/music.py` |
| **Local player** | `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/audio/music_player.py` (YouTube API, yt_dlp, VLC) |

**Endpoints**

- **None** toward FastAPI for music today.

**Env / config**

- `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` read in `music_player.py` (with **default key embedded in source** — should be removed when deleting this path).

---

## 4. Architectural mismatch analysis

1. **Different data sources:** Spotify catalog vs YouTube search.  
2. **Different engines:** Spotify Connect (cloud/device network) vs VLC (local process).  
3. **Different control paths:** Browser → FastAPI → Spotify vs Atlas orchestrator → Python VLC only.  
4. **Different state:** UI can poll `playback` / `status`; Atlas music does not update React or product API state.  
5. **Different user-visible behavior:** “Play X” in Atlas plays **YouTube audio locally**; same phrase in the product (after OAuth) plays **Spotify**.  
6. **Security / ops:** Hardcoded YouTube API default in `music_player.py` is a separate defect tied to the legacy path.

---

## 5. Canonical target model (per your decisions)

| Layer | Target |
|-------|--------|
| **Single canonical backend for music control** | **FastAPI** `backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py` (Spotify Web API only). |
| **Atlas** | Should **not** play audio locally. It should invoke the **same** operations the UI uses: HTTP to `{PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/api/spotify/...` with the same auth/session as the product (tokens already owned by FastAPI on disk). |
| **Frontend** | Keeps calling **`spotify.ts` → `/api/spotify/*`** unchanged in principle. |
| **Shared result / update behavior** | Playback state lives on **Spotify** + **FastAPI** token store; UI refreshes via existing polling; Atlas-triggered plays should produce the same Spotify-side state so **the next `playback` poll** matches (same as manual play). |
| **Old local player** | **`music_player.py` + YouTube/yt_dlp/VLC path removed** after Atlas tool is rewired; **`tools/music.py`** either deleted or reimplemented as HTTP adapter. |

---

## 6. Migration strategy

### Keep

- Entire **`spotify.py`** router and token persistence.  
- **`MusicMode.tsx`** / **`spotify.ts`** (minor tweaks only if you add “Atlas played” hints).  
- **Tool name `music`** (optional) for NLU continuity, **but implementation becomes HTTP to FastAPI**, not VLC.

### Adapt

- **`tool_executor.py`** `music` branch: instead of `execute_music_action` → `music_player`, call **`requests`** (or shared async helper) to:
  - `GET /api/spotify/search?q=...` then `POST /api/spotify/play` with `{ "uris": [...] }` for `play` + `song` query; or  
  - Add one **small** FastAPI helper e.g. `POST /api/spotify/play-track-query` `{ "q": "..." }` that does search+play server-side (fewer round trips, one place for “play by text”).  
- **`tools_registry.json`:** change `dependencies` from `["vlc","yt_dlp"]` to something like `["product_shell","internet"]`; update descriptions to **Spotify**.  
- **`tools/music.py`:** replace body with **FastAPI client** functions, or **delete** and inline in `tool_executor` (your choice in implementation phase).

### Deprecate / delete (after cutover)

- `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/audio/music_player.py`  
- YouTube-specific env usage in that module; remove **hardcoded API key**  
- **python-vlc**, **yt-dlp** as Atlas dependencies if nothing else uses them (verify with grep after removal)

---

## 7. UI / Atlas parity — direct API vs shell

| Option | Verdict |
|--------|---------|
| **Atlas → same Spotify HTTP API as UI (via FastAPI)** | **Recommended.** Reuses OAuth tokens, one playback domain, same Connect device, same `playback` polling behavior. |
| **Shell commands only** | **Poor fit:** there are **no** shell command kinds for Spotify in `ShellCommandListener.tsx` today; you’d have to add many commands and duplicate FastAPI logic in the browser. |
| **Hybrid** | Optional: **`cspe_set_mode` to `"music"`** so the user sees Music tab + **HTTP** play in parallel — UX only, not required for correctness. |

**Best for this repo:** **Atlas tools call FastAPI** (`PRODUCT_SHELL_URL`), same as `cspe_search_stops` calling `/v1/...`. No new shell music protocol required for parity.

---

## 8. Risks / blockers

| Risk | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Spotify Connect / active device** | `PUT /me/player/play` returns **404** if no active device — same for UI and Atlas; document “open Spotify on a device.” |
| **OAuth** | Tokens are tied to **FastAPI**; Atlas must **only** use HTTP to FastAPI (not duplicate OAuth in Atlas). |
| **LAN / origin** | If `PRODUCT_SHELL_URL` points across machines, ensure FastAPI reachable and CORS not required for **server-to-server** Atlas→FastAPI (requests from localhost Atlas to FastAPI — usually fine). |
| **Missing “play by query” one-shot** | Today UI searches then plays URI; Atlas tool only has `song` string — need **search + play** sequence or **one new endpoint** (see migration). |
| **Resume** | Spotify Web API resume is often “play” with same context; map Atlas `resume` to **`POST /api/spotify/play`** with empty body or documented behavior — verify against `spotify.py` (may need small adapter). |

---

## 9. Final recommendation

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **What are the two music systems today?** | **(1)** Product **Spotify via FastAPI** (`spotify.py` + React). **(2)** Atlas **YouTube + VLC** via `music_player.py` / tool `music`. |
| **What should the one system be?** | **Spotify-only music**, entirely driven through **`backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py`**, with Atlas invoking the **same HTTP surface** the UI uses (indirectly). |
| **First concrete implementation step** | **Replace** `execute_music_action` implementation to call **`{PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/api/spotify/search` + `/api/spotify/play`** (or add **`POST /api/spotify/play-query`**) and **map** `pause`/`next` to existing **`/api/spotify/pause`** and **`/api/spotify/next`**; then **delete `music_player.py`** and strip **vlc/yt_dlp** from tool metadata once verified. |

No refactor was performed in the repo beyond this analysis; the only “obvious” follow-up before coding is to decide between **two-step search+play** vs **one composite FastAPI endpoint** for Atlas ergonomics.

_**User**_

I want you to unify music in this repo so that Atlas and the manual UI both use the same Spotify-based music system, and remove the old Atlas local-player path completely.

Important context / decisions:
- Product memory and Atlas memory are intentionally separate and should NOT be merged.
- Music should be ONE system only.
- Spotify/product music is the canonical music system.
- The old Atlas YouTube + yt-dlp + VLC local music path must be removed.
- Atlas and the manual UI should become two ways to trigger the same music behavior.

Goal:
Perform the full music unification in one pass.
After your changes, music should flow through FastAPI/Spotify only, whether triggered manually in the UI or through Atlas.

Source of truth:
- Manual UI Spotify path already exists through FastAPI in backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py and frontend/src/api/spotify.ts / MusicMode.tsx.
- Atlas music currently uses tool "music" → tools/music.py → audio/music_player.py with YouTube/VLC local playback.
- We want Atlas to control the same Spotify backend the UI uses.

Your task:
Do the migration directly, not just analysis.

What to do:

1. Keep the Spotify system as the canonical music backend
- Reuse the existing FastAPI Spotify router and token persistence model.
- Do not create a second music backend.
- Do not duplicate OAuth logic inside Atlas.

2. Add the clean backend capability Atlas needs
Atlas currently has a “play by natural language query” behavior like “play song X”.
The current Spotify UI flow is more manual: search then pick/play.
To unify this properly, add a backend endpoint that supports Atlas ergonomics cleanly.

Preferred implementation:
- Add a FastAPI endpoint such as:
  - POST /api/spotify/play-query
or another clear name of your choice
- It should:
  - accept a text query
  - search Spotify
  - choose the best playable result
  - trigger playback using the same Spotify backend/token/device model
  - return a clear structured response (selected track, artist, uri/id if useful, success/failure, device/error context)

Also verify existing endpoints for:
- pause
- next
- playback state
- resume behavior
If a small adapter is needed for Atlas-friendly semantics, add it cleanly.

3. Rewire Atlas music tool to FastAPI
- Replace the old Atlas local music path so the tool no longer uses:
  - music_player.py
  - YouTube search
  - yt-dlp
  - VLC local playback
- Atlas music tool should call the FastAPI Spotify endpoints over HTTP using PRODUCT_SHELL_URL.
- Preserve the tool name "music" if useful for NLU continuity, but change its implementation to the FastAPI/Spotify path.
- Map actions like:
  - play(query)
  - pause
  - resume
  - next
to the appropriate FastAPI Spotify endpoints.

4. Remove the old local-player path
Once Atlas is fully rewired:
- remove or delete the old local music modules, including:
  - src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/audio/music_player.py
  - old Atlas music implementation that only exists for VLC/YouTube playback
- remove old references to:
  - yt-dlp
  - python-vlc
  - YouTube API search
  - YOUTUBE_API_KEY usage
- remove any hardcoded/default YouTube API key if still present anywhere
- clean tool metadata/dependencies accordingly

5. Keep the product UI working
Make sure the current manual Spotify UI still works:
- connect/login
- search
- play
- pause
- next
- status/playback polling
Do not break MusicMode.tsx / spotify.ts behavior.

6. Optional but recommended UI parity polish
If low-risk and clean:
- when Atlas triggers a music action, also enqueue a shell/UI command to switch to music mode or otherwise make the music state visible in the frontend
But this is secondary.
Correct Spotify backend unification matters more than UI mode auto-switching.

7. Update docs/config/comments
- Update tool descriptions and comments so they describe Spotify-based music, not local playback
- Remove misleading mentions of VLC/yt-dlp/YouTube if obsolete
- Clean env/config references accordingly

8. Safety / verification
Before deleting the old path, make sure Atlas can:
- play by query through Spotify
- pause
- resume
- next
and that failures are handled clearly (for example no active Spotify device, no auth, no search result)

After migration, verify:
- frontend music still works
- Atlas music uses FastAPI/Spotify only
- no local playback path remains active
- no obsolete references to YouTube/VLC remain in the active architecture

Expected deliverables:
1. Apply the code changes directly
2. Then provide a concise migration report with:

- files removed

- Atlas tool changes
- removed dependencies / removed env usage
- any manual follow-up needed
- short “post-migration music architecture” summary

Rules:
- Do not introduce a second music system
- Do not keep compatibility shims for local playback unless absolutely necessary
- Do not duplicate Spotify auth/state management inside Atlas
- Keep architecture clean: one music backend, two input modes (manual UI and Atlas)

Spotify via FastAPI,
used both by the manual UI and by Atlas,

## Migration report — unified Spotify music

### Files added
- None (logic added inside existing `spotify.py`).

### Files modified
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py` | Added `PlayQueryBody`, `_playback_hint`, **`POST /api/spotify/play-query`** (search → first track → `PUT /me/player/play`), returns structured `{ok, error?, track?, ...}` without always raising HTTP errors. |
| `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/tools/music.py` | Replaced YouTube/VLC with **HTTP** to `{PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}`: `/api/spotify/play-query`, `/pause`, `/play` (resume), `/next`; **`stop` → pause**; optional **`next`**; deferred play after TTS unchanged (async task). |
| `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tools_registry.json` | Tool **`music`**: Spotify wording, **`next`** in enum, dependencies **`["product_shell", "spotify_account"]`**. |

### Files removed
| File |
|------|
| `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/audio/music_player.py` (YouTube API + yt-dlp + VLC) |

### New / updated FastAPI endpoints
| Method | Path | Role |
|--------|------|------|
| **POST** | **`/api/spotify/play-query`** | Body `{ "query": "<text>" }` → Spotify search (tracks, limit 10) → play **first** hit → returns `{ ok, query, track? }` or `{ ok: false, error, message?, hint?, spotify_status? }`. |

Existing **`/api/spotify/play`**, **`/pause`**, **`/next`**, **`/playback`**, etc. unchanged for the React UI.

### Atlas tool changes
- **`music`** still calls `execute_music_action` from `tool_executor.py` (no change there).
- Implementation now uses **`requests`** to the product API only (no local player, no OAuth in Atlas).

### Removed dependencies / env (effective)
- **Removed from runtime:** VLC, yt-dlp, YouTube search, **`YOUTUBE_API_KEY`** (including the old hardcoded default in `music_player.py`).
- **Not in root `requirements.txt`:** those packages were never listed there; remove them from an **Atlas `.venv`** if they were installed manually.

### Manual follow-up
1. **Spotify login in the app** (Music mode) so `data/spotify_tokens.json` exists — Atlas uses the **same** FastAPI-backed session.
2. **`PRODUCT_SHELL_URL`** must point at the running product API (default `http://127.0.0.1:8787`), including for Atlas subprocesses (e.g. set in `run_web_app.ps1` — already defaults this).
3. **Active Spotify Connect device** still required for play/pause/next (unchanged Spotify Web API behavior).

### Post-migration music architecture (short)
- **Single music stack:** Spotify Web API via **`backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py`** (tokens on disk + in-memory).
- **UI:** unchanged (`spotify.ts` / `MusicMode.tsx`).
- **Atlas:** tool **`music`** → HTTP to **`/api/spotify/*`** on the product shell, including **`/api/spotify/play-query`** for “play &lt;natural query&gt;”.
- **No** local YouTube/VLC path remains in the repo.

_**User**_

I want you to unify transport in this repo so that Atlas and the manual UI trigger the same transport actions and produce the same visible result in the frontend.

Important context / decisions:
- Streamlit is already removed.
- cspe_api is already merged into FastAPI.
- Music is already unified on Spotify and the old local Atlas music path is removed.
- Product memory and Atlas memory are intentionally separate and should NOT be merged.
- Transport should be ONE product action system.
- Atlas and the manual UI are two input modes for the same transport behavior.
- If a user searches a stop or computes a route manually or by asking Atlas, the frontend should end up showing the same result: same stop/path semantics, same map behavior, same UI state.

Goal:
Perform the transport unification in one pass.
After your changes, transport should have one canonical backend action pipeline and Atlas should use that same product transport behavior instead of a parallel /v1-style semantics.

What I want conceptually:
- one canonical transport search behavior
- one canonical transport route behavior
- one canonical map update/display behavior
- frontend manual UI and Atlas commands should converge to the same result
- no long-term split between "/api/transport/*" and Atlas-only transport semantics

Your task:
Do the migration directly, not just analysis.

What to do:

1. Define and implement canonical transport actions
Unify the backend behavior for:
- stop/station search
- route computation
- map update/render behavior

I want one clear canonical product transport pipeline.
If there is a useful distinction between stop-level and station-level internally, keep it internally, but expose one coherent product behavior.

2. Remove the transport semantic split between UI and Atlas
Right now the audit showed:
- UI uses /api/transport/stops/search and /api/transport/route
- Atlas uses /v1/search_stops and /v1/route
- they currently use different helpers / shapes / semantics

Fix this so Atlas no longer follows a separate transport logic path.

Preferred direction:
- Atlas tools should use the same canonical transport backend actions as the manual UI
- if needed, keep temporary compatibility wrappers only internally, but the active architecture should clearly converge on one transport contract

3. Unify search behavior
Manual UI and Atlas should not use different autocomplete semantics long-term.
Choose and implement the canonical search behavior for the product.
Then make both:
- manual UI search
- Atlas stop search / route resolution
use that same logic.

Be explicit in code and cleanup:
- remove duplicate transport search paths if obsolete
- align response models if needed
- keep the result useful for both UI and Atlas

4. Unify route behavior
Manual UI and Atlas should not get different route result models for the same transport task.
Create one canonical backend route action/result model suitable for:
- frontend rendering
- Atlas interpretation
- map update

If Atlas needs a lighter adapter internally, keep that adapter thin, but the underlying action/result should be the same as the product route behavior.

5. Unify map outcome
This is critical:
When Atlas triggers a transport action, the frontend should end up showing the same stop/path/map result as if the user had done it manually.

So make sure Atlas-driven transport actions lead to the same frontend state transitions and map refresh behavior as manual UI transport actions.

Do not leave Atlas in a state where it computes a route “in theory” but the visible map/UI outcome is different or incomplete.

6. Decide the correct role of shell commands in transport
Use shell commands only where they make architectural sense:
- for UI state/navigation/mode switching
- for declarative application of transport results to frontend state if needed

But do not keep a split where:
- UI gets transport data one way
- Atlas gets transport data another way
- shell commands only partially mirror the result

I want one coherent model.

7. Clean up obsolete transport compatibility paths
After unification:
- remove or deprecate obsolete /v1 transport semantics if they are no longer needed
- remove dead code, dead adapters, dead comments, dead docs, dead tool assumptions
- keep the repo behavior clear and coherent

If keeping a temporary compatibility endpoint is the safest migration step, that is acceptable only if:
- the underlying logic is the same
- the architecture clearly has one canonical transport pipeline
- the compatibility layer is thin and clearly marked

8. Preserve the UI and product behavior
Make sure the existing React transport UI still works:
- stop search
- route computation
- map rendering
- stats if relevant
- mode behavior
Do not break the manual UI while unifying Atlas onto it.

9. Update Atlas transport tools
Update Atlas tools so they use the unified transport model.
This may involve:
- changing which FastAPI endpoints they call
- changing response parsing
- changing how shell commands are emitted afterward
- using canonical transport results instead of legacy raw shortest_path-style responses

10. Verification
After the change, verify these scenarios conceptually and in code:
- manual UI stop search works
- Atlas stop search resolves the same type of result
- manual UI route works
- Atlas route leads to the same visible frontend transport result
- map behavior is consistent
- no parallel transport semantics remain in active use unless explicitly justified and thin

Expected deliverables:
1. Apply the code changes directly
2. Then provide a concise migration report with:
- files added
- files modified
- files removed
- which endpoint(s) are now canonical for transport
- Atlas tool changes
- shell command changes if any
- any compatibility path temporarily kept
- anything needing manual follow-up
- short “post-migration transport architecture” summary

Rules:
- Do not just patch the symptom; fix the architecture
- Do not keep two competing transport result models long-term
- Do not break the React + FastAPI + Atlas workflow
- Keep transport as a domain/service boundary behind FastAPI, not a blob in route handlers
- Atlas and manual UI should become two ways to trigger the same transport behavior

Success condition:
After your changes, transport in this repo should behave like one product system:
manual UI and Atlas use the same canonical backend transport actions,
and the frontend shows the same resulting stop/path/map behavior regardless of how the action was triggered.

Here is what was implemented to finish the transport unification (continuing from the prior handoff).

## Migration report

### Added
- **`GET /api/transport/bundle-health`** in `backend/product_shell/routers/transport.py` — exposes `transport_engine.get_bundle()` metadata (`cache_version`, graph `modes`) so graph readiness is not tied to a separate `/v1` surface.

### Modified
- **`backend/product_shell/main.py`** — dropped `v1_graph` router include (no parallel `/v1/*` transport API).
- **`src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tool_executor.py`**
  - **`cspe_search_stops`** → **`GET {PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/api/transport/stops/search`** with `q`, `limit`, `mode`, `use_lcc`, `station_first` (same query model as the React `searchStops` helper).
  - **`cspe_route`** → **`POST …/api/transport/route`** with the same `TransportRouteRequest` shape as the UI (stop pair **or** station pair, not both).
  - After each route, **enqueues shell commands** so the frontend matches manual behavior: `set_mode` → `transport` → `transport_graph_mode` → `transport_options` (`use_lcc` + `graph_viz` from `routing_scope`) → `transport_route_view` (paths + `route_meta` / clear + `route_error` on failure).
  - Helpers: `_get_http`, `_format_transport_route_meta` (aligned with `TransportMode`’s route summary line).
- **`src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tools_registry.json`** — documents `/api/transport/*`, optional `use_lcc` / `station_first` for search, optional station endpoints for `cspe_route`, outputs `matches` + `stops` alias and `route`.
- **`run_web_app.ps1`** — comment updated (no `/v1` transport mention).

### Removed
- **`backend/product_shell/routers/v1_graph.py`**
- **`backend/product_shell/services/cspe_v1_graph.py`**

### Canonical transport HTTP API (single pipeline)
| Action | Endpoint |
|--------|----------|
| Stop/station search | **`GET /api/transport/stops/search`** |
| Route | **`POST /api/transport/route`** |
| Map HTML | **`POST /api/transport/map`** |
| Stats | **`GET /api/transport/stats`** |
| Bundle readiness | **`GET /api/transport/bundle-health`** |

All of these go through **`transport_engine`** (same as the manual UI).

### Atlas tool behavior
- **`cspe_search_stops`**: product search only; returns `{ matches, stops, … }` (no `/v1` POST).
- **`cspe_route`**: product route only; **`data.route`** is the canonical **`TransportRouteResponse`** JSON; **`shell_enqueued: true`** when enqueue succeeds so the map/state updates like a manual route.

### Shell command changes
- **`cspe_route`** now always drives **`set_mode`**, **`transport_graph_mode`**, **`transport_options`**, and **`transport_route_view`** after a route call so Zustand + `TransportMode`’s `refreshMap` path stay in sync with the API result.

### Compatibility
- **No** thin `/v1` compatibility layer — removed. Atlas and UI both use **`/api/transport/*`** only.

### Manual follow-up
- Run the stack in an environment with **FastAPI installed** and smoke-test: UI search/route, Atlas `cspe_search_stops` / `cspe_route`, and confirm the shell poll applies path + meta (this workspace’s default `python` had no `fastapi`, so the app import was not executed here).
- **`cspe_route` tool receipt `ok`** is **`False`** when the graph returns no route (logical failure), even if HTTP 200 — intended so the model sees failure; shell still clears paths and sets **`route_error`**.

### Post-migration architecture (short)
**One product transport domain** behind FastAPI: **`transport_engine`** + **`/api/transport/*`**. The React app and Atlas tools are **two clients** of that API; Atlas additionally uses **`/api/shell/enqueue`** to push the same route/search-related **UI state** the manual flow would set (graph mode, LCC, stop vs station viz, path IDs, errors, meta). No second routing semantics or duplicate result models for active transport.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here is what was going wrong and what we changed.

## Cause

`cspe_search_stops` calls:

`{PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/api/transport/stops/search?...`

If **`PRODUCT_SHELL_URL` is set with a trailing `/api`** (for example `http://127.0.0.1:8787/api`), the URL becomes:

`http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/api/transport/stops/search`

FastAPI has no route for that path, so you get **`404` with `"detail": "Not Found"`** — not a bad query string.

## Fix

1. **`product_shell_origin()`** in `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/core/config.py`  
   - Reads `PRODUCT_SHELL_URL` and **strips a trailing `/api`** (case-insensitive) so callers can safely append `/api/...`.

2. **`tool_executor.py`** — `_product_shell_base()` now uses `product_shell_origin()`.

3. **`music.py`** — same base helper (Spotify calls were subject to the same bug).

4. **Clearer errors** — on failed stop search, the tool receipt includes **`request_url`** and **`product_shell_base`** so logs show the exact URL. For **404**, the error text mentions fixing `PRODUCT_SHELL_URL`.

5. **`run_web_app.ps1`** — comment updated: use the API **origin only**, no trailing `/api`.

## What you should do

- Prefer: `PRODUCT_SHELL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787` (or your real host/port **without** `/api`).
- If you had `.../8787/api`, remove the `/api` **or** rely on the new normalizer (either works now).

After pulling these changes, retry `cspe_search_stops`; it should hit **`/api/transport/stops/search`** once and return matches when the product API is up on 8787.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


`play_after_tts` was missing from `music.py` (it isn’t defined there anymore, but `orchestrator.py` still imports it for the music tool path that runs Spotify **after** TTS).

Restored it as an async helper that:

1. Waits while `state.playback_active` is true (same idea as the deferred branch inside `execute_music_action`).
2. Calls `execute_music_action("play", q, state=None)` so playback hits the product API immediately, without queuing another “after TTS” task.

```18:34:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/tools/music.py
async def play_after_tts(state: Any, song: str) -> None:
    """Wait until assistant TTS is no longer active, then play ``song`` via the product Spotify API."""
    q = (song or "").strip()
    if not q:
        return
    try:
        while getattr(state, "playback_active", False):
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        raise
    except Exception:
        pass
    r = await execute_music_action("play", q, state=None)
    if not r.get("ok"):
        LOG.warning("[music] play_after_tts failed: %s", r.get("error"))
```

Run `.\run_web_app.ps1` again; the Atlas API import chain should load past `orchestrator` → `music`.

Here’s what’s going on, in plain terms:

**Python is doing:** “Load `music.py` and give me something named `play_after_tts`.”

**What actually happens:** That module finishes loading **without** defining anything called `play_after_tts` (or the version you’re running never got that addition).

So the failure is a **missing export**: `orchestrator.py` line 39 says `from ..tools.music import play_after_tts`, but **`play_after_tts` is not a name that exists on `music.py` in the copy of the repo that Atlas is using.**

Common reasons (pick what fits your situation):

1. **The fix wasn’t saved / wasn’t pulled** — the file on disk still doesn’t define `play_after_tts`.
2. **Different environment** — you’re running from another checkout or branch where `music.py` was never updated.
3. **Rare:** the name exists in an editor buffer but not on disk, or you’re editing a different `music.py` than the one under `src\work\atlas\src\atlas_client\tools\`.

**It is not** a “wrong PYTHONPATH” or “wrong venv” issue by itself — those would usually fail on `atlas_client` entirely. Here the module loads; only **that one symbol** is missing.

**What to verify (no coding, just check):** Open `C:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\src\work\atlas\src\atlas_client\tools\music.py` and confirm there is a **function (or assignment) literally named `play_after_tts`** in that file. If it’s not there, that’s the problem.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Implementing music player stop**

I'm adding a helper function to extract the product shell origin from environment variables, ensuring it strips trailing slashes and handles missing env vars gracefully. 

**Adding config variable**

I'm adding product_shell_origin to config.py to avoid duplicate logic in music_player.py. I'm adding product_shell_origin to config.py and exporting music_player from audio.__init__.py. 

I'm exporting music_player from audio.__init__.py to make it importable as a submodule. I need to add `music_player` to `audio.__init__.py` to resolve the ImportError. I'm creating `music_player.py` with `stop_song()` function and updating `audio.__init__.py` to import it. 

**Creating music player module**

I'm creating `audio/music_player.py` with the `stop_song()` function and `_origin()` helper. I'm implementing the `stop_song()` function to pause Spotify via API call. 

**Updating audio module**

I'm updating the audio module's __init__.py to re-export the music_player module. I discovered that Python automatically loads submodules if they're not in __init__.py, so I don't need to explicitly re-export `azure_tts_player`. 

I confirmed that Python 3.3+ allows implicit namespace packages, so submodules like `azure_tts_player` and `music_player` don't need to be explicitly exported in `__init__.py`. I confirmed that importing submodules like `music_player` works without editing `__init__.py` in Python 3. </details></think>

Here’s what was wrong and what we did.

**Cause:** Local playback was removed in favor of Spotify, but `orchestrator.py` still does `from ..audio import music_player` and calls `music_player.stop_song()` in the `finally` block when a session ends. There was no `music_player` module anymore, so the import failed.

**Change:** Added `src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/audio/music_player.py` with a **`stop_song()`** that sends a best-effort **`POST` to `{PRODUCT_SHELL_URL}/api/spotify/pause`** (with the same trailing `/api` stripping as your transport fix), so teardown pauses Spotify instead of touching a removed local player.

Run `.\run_web_app.ps1` again; the Atlas API should import cleanly.

Here is what was wrong and what we changed.

## What was wrong
In **Stations** (and **Both**) view, markers come from the **`station-net-points`** layer. That GeoJSON only had `station_id`, `name`, and `is_selected` — **no** `hover_html`, `click_html`, or `nearby_pois_json`. The map script only wired **hover/click/POI popups** to the **`stations`** layer (stop markers), so station dots never got the same behavior.

## What we did

1. **`src/viz/plot_mapbox.py`**
   - **`_nearby_pois_at_lon_lat`** – POIs around a lon/lat (centroid).
   - **`_merge_lines_for_station_group`**, **`_station_group_degree_sum`** – aggregate platforms at an interchange.
   - **`_station_group_hover_html`** / **`_station_group_click_html_with_pois`** – interchange card: modes/lines, platform list, **Nearby POIs** (same idea as stop popups).
   - **`_enrich_station_network_points_fc`** – fills `hover_html`, `click_html`, `nearby_pois_json`, and helper fields on each station point.
   - **`render_mapbox_gl_html(..., station_layer_index=...)`** – after building station points, runs enrichment when a **`StationLayerIndex`** is passed.
   - **Mapbox JS** – `bindStationPopupFromFeature` shared by stops and stations; **`station-net-points`** gets the same `mouseenter` / `mouseleave` / `mousemove` / `click` behavior as **`stations`**; background click clears popups for **both** layers.
   - **CSS** – `.station-platform-list`, `.station-platform-row`, `.station-platform-id` for the platform list.
   - **`buildLightHoverHtml`** – uses `station_name` when present.

2. **`backend/product_shell/transport_engine.py`**
   - Passes **`station_layer_index=idx`** whenever the map is not pure stop-only (`gv != "stop"`), so **Stations**, **Both**, and route-only station overlays all get enriched points.

After a refresh, **clicking a station** on the map should show the interchange-style card and **nearby POIs** (and map POI pins), consistent with stop selection.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s where those actions show up:

**1. Product API (FastAPI) process**  
Transport search and route requests go to the server you start with **`run_web_app.ps1`** (uvicorn on port **8787**). That process’s **console output** is the main place you’ll see **HTTP access lines** (method, URL path, status) for calls like `/api/transport/stops/search` and `/api/transport/route`. If it was started in a **minimized** window, bring that terminal/window to the front to read it.

**2. Optional debug log file**  
Some parts of the stack (including map/render code that uses the shared debug logger) append to **`logs/cspe_debug.log`** at the **repo root**. That’s more about **map/render / internal events** than a full audit of every UI click, but it’s worth checking if you care about map-side logging.

**3. Browser (not server logs)**  
In **DevTools → Network**, you can see the same requests and responses the UI makes. That’s for inspection, not server log files.

**Not used for plain UI transport:** Atlas logs under **`src/work/atlas/logs/`** are for the **Atlas** process (voice/chat), not for you typing in the React transport UI unless something else is wired to them.

**Short answer:** Use the **uvicorn/FastAPI terminal** for request-level visibility; use **`logs/cspe_debug.log`** if you’ve enabled or triggered debug logging for map/render; use the **browser Network** tab to see exact API calls from the UI.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


**`logs/cspe_debug.log`** is a **rotating debug log file** (about 2 MB per chunk, a few backups) written by the shared **`cspe`** logger.

In this repo it’s effectively the **map rendering / Mapbox pipeline log**: code in **`plot_mapbox.py`** records **structured JSON lines** (via `log_event`) for things like basemap URL normalization, Paris mask load/skip, and **`render_mapbox_payload_built`** (mode, zoom, feature counts, POI index loaded, etc.). It’s **not** a general “every API request from the UI” log—those show up on the **uvicorn console** unless other code starts using the same logger elsewhere.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


## Diagnosis summary

Station routing in the **backend** does **not** treat `from_station_id` / `to_station_id` as free text. It looks them up as **keys** in `StationLayerIndex.station_to_stops` for the **same** `(mode, use_lcc)` graph used for routing. The **UI** almost always sends **IDs returned by `transport.search_stops`**. **Atlas** often sends **human names** (or typos) straight into `cspe_route`, which bypasses that lookup—so `"gare de l'est"` is not a valid station key unless it coincidentally matches a partition id (it does not). The registry text even tells the model to **search first**, but nothing in code enforces a search→route pipeline.

---

## UI flow vs Atlas flow

| Step | UI (Transport mode) | Atlas |
|------|------------------------|--------|
| **Resolve names → IDs** | Yes, by design: autocomplete calls **`GET /api/transport/stops/search`** with `q`, `mode`, `use_lcc`, `station_first`. User picks a row; **`startId` / `endId`** are set from **`s.station_id`** or **`s.stop_id`** (see `TransportMode.tsx` suggestion `onClick` and `computeRoute` using those ids). | **Not automatic.** The model may call **`cspe_search_stops`** first, but **`cspe_route`** is a **separate** tool call. The executor **does not** run search before route; it forwards **`from_station_id` / `to_station_id` strings** from the model **unchanged** into **`POST /api/transport/route`** (`tool_executor.py` builds the JSON payload from args). |
| **Route request** | **`postRoute(graphMode, useLcc, { kind: "station", from_station_id, to_station_id })`** — ids come from search matches, aligned with current **graph mode + LCC + station-first** (`TransportMode.tsx` ~171–185, `client.ts`). | Same HTTP contract, but **args are whatever the router/model outputs** (your logs show **plain names** in `from_station_id` / `to_station_id`). |
| **Backend behavior** | **`compute_route_stations`** uses `idx.station_to_stops.get(from_station_id, [])` — expects **canonical station keys** for that index (`transport_engine.py` ~297–300). Empty → **"Start station not found in the current graph."** | Same code path → same error when the string is not a key. |

So: **same backend**, **same endpoint**, **different inputs**: UI supplies **resolved canonical ids**; Atlas often supplies **unresolved labels**.

---

## Confirmed causes (supported by code)

1. **Station routing expects canonical station ids, not display names.**  
   - Evidence: `compute_route_stations` only does `idx.station_to_stops.get(fs, [])` with **no name resolution** (`transport_engine.py` ~295–300).  
   - API contract: `TransportRouteRequest` fields are literally `from_station_id` / `to_station_id` (opaque strings); Pydantic does not interpret them as names (`schemas.py` ~43–51).

2. **Atlas skips an enforced resolution step between name and route.**  
   - Evidence: `cspe_route` builds the POST body **directly** from tool args (`tool_executor.py` ~565–595). There is **no** call to `cspe_search_stops` inside `cspe_route`.  
   - Registry **suggests** “After resolving names via cspe_search_stops” (`tools_registry.json` ~751–753), but that is **only model instructions**, not executor logic.

3. **Graph context (mode + `use_lcc`) defines which station ids exist.**  
   - Evidence: `station_layer_for(mode, use_lcc)` builds the index from `graph_for(mode, use_lcc)` (`transport_engine.py` ~115–118, ~295–296). Different graphs/partitions ⇒ **different `station_to_stops` keys**.  
   - Your observation (e.g. Opéra / Gare de l’Est mapping to **different** `st:IDFM:…` when `use_lcc` flips) is **consistent** with ids being **bundle/partition-dependent**, not universal names.

---

## Possible / contributing causes (need your confirmation)

1. **Model passes names into `*_station_id` despite instructions** — behavior of the semantic router + LLM, not verifiable from static code alone; your pasted logs are the evidence.

2. **Decorated labels break search** — if the UI sends **`q`** like `"Opéra · Lines 3, 8, 7"`, **`search_stops`** may return **0 matches** depending on how `search_stations_autocomplete` tokenizes (you already observed 0 results). That’s a **search-query** issue, separate from route, but it forces bad manual input.

3. **Default `use_lcc` mismatch UI vs API default** — `TransportRouteRequest` defaults **`use_lcc=True`** in `schemas.py` (~47); the UI store defaults **`transportUseLcc: false`** (`store.ts` ~96). Atlas tool default **`false`** in registry. A route logged with **`use_lcc: true`** is consistent with UI toggling LCC or API default when omitted—not a contradiction by itself, but **any** search done with one flag and route with another can yield **different** canonical ids for the “same” place.

---

## Route backend contract (station routing)

**Yes: it expects ids that are valid keys for the active station layer** (canonical partition ids like `st:IDFM:…` in your data), **not** human-readable names. There is **no** secondary resolver inside `compute_route_stations` for free text.

---

## Second issue: ids depend on graph context

**Yes, supported by code:** `StationLayerIndex` is tied to **`graph_for(mode, use_lcc)`**. Resolving a station under one `(mode, use_lcc)` and routing under another can use **different** keys for the same toponym—your Opéra / Gare de l’Est examples are exactly what this structure predicts.

---

## What to verify before fixing (no code)

1. **Atlas traces:** For a failing route, confirm whether **`cspe_search_stops` was called in the same turn** and whether the model copied **`station_id`** from its **JSON** (with `st:IDFM:…`) into **`cspe_route`** or pasted **natural language** into `from_station_id` / `to_station_id`.

2. **Align flags:** For the same session, log **`mode`, `use_lcc`, `station_first`** on **both** search and route (UI already pairs them; Atlas must match per turn).

3. **Reproduce id drift:** Call **`transport.search_stops`** with **`use_lcc: false`**, note `station_id`, then **`transport.route`** with the **same** id but **`use_lcc: true`** (or the reverse) and confirm failure if ids differ across layers.

4. **Product UI log** (`product_ui_transport.log`): Compare **`transport.search_stops`** previews vs **`transport.route`** args for successful UI runs to establish the **canonical id** pattern you expect Atlas to mimic.

---

**Bottom line:** The main issue is **not** “two different backends”—it is **Atlas supplying unresolved names (or wrong ids) as station ids**, plus **optional context mismatch** (`mode` / `use_lcc`) between search and route. The backend contract is **canonical station keys only** for station routing; names are **not** interpreted there.

---

_**User**_

I have runtime evidence that routing works when canonical station_ids are used, and fails when names are passed.

3. Confirm that `cspe_route` in tool_executor forwards args without resolving names.

## Confirmed behaviors (code)

### 1) `POST /api/transport/route` does not resolve station names; it passes strings straight into `compute_route_stations`

The handler strips request fields and, for station routing, calls `compute_route_stations(fs, ts, ...)` with those strings unchanged—no search or name lookup in between:

```88:104:backend/product_shell/routers/transport.py
def post_transport_route(body: TransportRouteRequest) -> TransportRouteResponse:
    try:
        fs, ts = (body.from_station_id or "").strip(), (body.to_station_id or "").strip()
        fa, tb = (body.from_stop_id or "").strip(), (body.to_stop_id or "").strip()
        has_st = bool(fs and ts)
        has_sp = bool(fa and tb)
        if has_st == has_sp:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=400,
                detail="Provide exactly one of: (from_stop_id, to_stop_id) or (from_station_id, to_station_id).",
            )
        if has_st:
            r = te.compute_route_stations(fs, ts, mode=body.mode, use_lcc=body.use_lcc)
            routing = "station"
        else:
            r = te.compute_route(fa, tb, mode=body.mode, use_lcc=body.use_lcc)
```

The request model only declares opaque optional ids—no semantics that they are names (`schemas.py`):

```43:51:backend/product_shell/schemas.py
class TransportRouteRequest(BaseModel):
    """Either stop endpoints (from_stop_id + to_stop_id) or station endpoints (from_station_id + to_station_id)."""

    mode: Literal["all", "metro", "rail", "tram", "bus", "other"] = "metro"
    use_lcc: bool = True
    from_stop_id: str | None = None
    to_stop_id: str | None = None
    from_station_id: str | None = None
    to_station_id: str | None = None
```

So the **contract** is: station endpoints are whatever strings the client sends; the **implementation** treats them as **keys** into `station_to_stops` (below), not as human-readable names to resolve.

---

### 2) `compute_route_stations` uses `station_to_stops` as a dict keyed by station id; arbitrary names miss and fail at start/end

```290:314:backend/product_shell/transport_engine.py
def compute_route_stations(
    from_station_id: str, to_station_id: str, *, mode: str, use_lcc: bool
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from src.core.queries import component_info, summarize_path

    G = graph_for(mode, use_lcc)
    idx = station_layer_for(mode, use_lcc)
    fs, ts = str(from_station_id).strip(), str(to_station_id).strip()

    a_stops = [s for s in idx.station_to_stops.get(fs, []) if s in G]
    b_stops = [s for s in idx.station_to_stops.get(ts, []) if s in G]
    if not a_stops:
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "routing_scope": "station",
            ...
            "error": {
                "message": "Start station not found in the current graph.",
                ...
                "reason": "start_station_not_found",
            },
        }
```

**Why names fail:** `station_to_stops.get(fs, [])` only returns platforms if `fs` is **exactly** a key in `station_to_stops`. A free-text label like `"gare de l'est"` is not normalized or looked up—so lookup returns `[]`, `a_stops` is empty, and the **start_station_not_found** branch runs.

There is **no** call to `search_stops` / `search_stations_autocomplete` inside `compute_route_stations` (the only `search_stops` usage in this layer is the separate `search_stops` function in the same module for the search API).

---

```565:598:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tool_executor.py
        elif name == "cspe_route":
            a = str(args.get("from_stop_id") or "").strip()
            b = str(args.get("to_stop_id") or "").strip()
            sa = str(args.get("from_station_id") or "").strip()

            else:

                }
            base = _product_shell_base()
            url = f"{base}/api/transport/route"
            resp, net_err = await _post_json_http(url, payload, 45.0)
```

No `cspe_search_stops` (or any resolver) runs in this branch before the POST.

### 4) No backend/executor fallback to resolve station names for routing

- **Callers of `compute_route_stations`:** only `post_transport_route` (see grep: `transport.py` + definition in `transport_engine.py`).
- **`compute_route_stations`:** only uses `graph_for`, `station_layer_for`, and `idx.station_to_stops.get(...)`—no name resolution path (see block above).

So there is **no** alternate path in the product shell that turns a display name into a station key before routing.

---

### 5) `StationLayerIndex` is tied to `(mode, use_lcc)` via `graph_for` → `build_station_layer`

```115:119:backend/product_shell/transport_engine.py
@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
def station_layer_for(mode: str, use_lcc: bool) -> StationLayerIndex:
    """Cached station grouping for the active stop graph (routing stays stop-level)."""
    G = graph_for(mode, use_lcc)
    return build_station_layer(G, project_root=ROOT)
```

```107:112:backend/product_shell/transport_engine.py
def graph_for(mode: str, use_lcc: bool) -> Any:
    bundle = get_bundle()
    graphs = bundle["graphs"]
    graphs_lcc = bundle["graphs_lcc"]
    G = (graphs_lcc if use_lcc else graphs)[mode]
    return G
```

So the **same** `(mode, use_lcc)` pair selects both the graph `G` and the station partition `idx`. Keys in `station_to_stops` are whatever `build_station_layer` assigns for **that** `G`; changing `mode` or `use_lcc` can change `G` and thus the station index (consistent with your runtime observation that canonical ids differ across LCC).

The index structure is defined in `StationLayerIndex` (`station_to_stops` maps station id → stop ids):

```26:34:src/core/station_layer.py
@dataclass
class StationLayerIndex:
    """station_id -> child stop_ids; each stop maps to exactly one station."""

    stop_to_station: dict[str, str]
    station_to_stops: dict[str, list[str]]
    station_label: dict[str, str]
    station_centroid: dict[str, tuple[float, float]]  # lon, lat
```

That affects **which graph** is used, not whether a **string** is treated as a name—it does not add name resolution.

## 1) Single utterance: search first → route second, or names straight into `cspe_route`?

**Atlas does not chain `cspe_search_stops` → `cspe_route` in one routing step.**

The semantic router is instructed to output **exactly one** tool per decision:

```38:40:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/core/semantic_router.py
You must choose EXACTLY ONE:
1) DIRECT answer (no tool)
2) TOOL call (choose ONE tool and its args)
```

For a line like “compute a path between A and B”, `route_semantic` returns **one** `RouteDecision` with **one** `tool_name` and **one** `args` object. The orchestrator then builds a **single** tool call and executes it—there is no loop that runs search and then route for the same user line:

```524:526:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/core/orchestrator.py
            tool_calls = [{"name": decision.tool_name, "args": tool_args}]

            await record_timestamp(turn_id, "tool_exec_start", time.monotonic())
```

So if the router chooses **`cspe_route`**, the model fills **`from_station_id` / `to_station_id`** (or stop ids) **directly** from the utterance. There is **no** automatic prior `cspe_search_stops` in that turn.

**Confirmed:** the failure mode “names in `*_station_id`” is introduced at **router output / tool-argument generation**, not at HTTP or executor wiring.

---

## 2) If `cspe_search_stops` ran earlier, where is `station_id` lost?

**There is no code path that copies search **results** (with `station_id`) into a later `cspe_route` call.**

- After any tool run, context is updated with **`last_tool`**, **`last_tool_args`** (the **args passed into** `execute_tool`, e.g. `{query: ...}` for search), and a **text** **`last_tool_result`** taken from the receipt **summary** string—not full JSON:

```568:571:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/core/orchestrator.py
            if tool_receipts:
                summary = (tool_receipts[-1].get("summary") or "").strip()
                if summary:
                    await update_router_context(last_tool_result=summary)
```

- The router’s **`CONTEXT`** string only includes a **short** `LAST_TOOL_RESULT` (first 200 chars of that summary), not structured `matches[].station_id`:

```277:303:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/core/session_state.py
async def format_router_context_summary(max_chars: int = 700) -> str:
    ...
    if last_tool_result:
        parts.append(f"LAST_TOOL_RESULT: {last_tool_result[:200]}")
```

So even if a **previous** turn called `cspe_search_stops` and returned canonical ids in the tool payload, **those ids are not stored as structured router state** for the next `cspe_route`. The next turn’s router must infer args again from text + this thin context.

**If `station_id` is “lost”, it is at the layer of: no structured handoff from search results → route args** (not a bug inside `tool_executor` alone).

---

## 3) Does the router / prompt encourage direct `cspe_route` with raw names?

- **Router system prompt** says to use **`cspe_search_stops` and/or `cspe_route`** for Paris transit graph tasks—**“and/or”** does not require search before route:

```63:64:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/core/semantic_router.py
- PARIS / ÎLE-DE-FRANCE TRANSIT (CSPE graph): For stop/station lookup, metro/RER/tram/bus routes between stops in the CSPE dataset, or graph connectivity, use cspe_search_stops and/or cspe_route.
```

- **`tools_registry.json`** tells the catalog that **`cspe_route`** should be used **after** resolving names via search—but that text is only part of the **tool description** fed to the router as catalog lines, not enforced:

```751:753:src/work/atlas/src/atlas_client/router/tools_registry.json
      "when_to_use": [
        "User asks for a route, connection, or how to go between two specific stations in the CSPE graph",
        "After resolving names via cspe_search_stops (use station IDs when station_first search, else stop IDs)"
```

So the **LLM router** can still output **`cspe_route`** with **place names** in `*_station_id` fields in one shot; nothing in code blocks that.

**Classification:** **tool-argument generation** (and routing choice between one tool vs two-step behavior), not backend.

---

## 4) Same `mode` / `use_lcc` between search and route **in one turn**?

**In a single user utterance, only one tool runs**, so there is **no** pair (search, route) to align—only whatever **`mode` / `use_lcc`** the router puts in **`cspe_route`** (defaults in executor: `mode` default `"metro"`, `use_lcc` default `False` if omitted—see `tool_executor.py` ~580–581).

Across **turns**, context does **not** carry prior `use_lcc` / `station_first` from `cspe_search_stops` as dedicated fields; the next decision is a **new** `args` object from **`route_semantic`** again.

---

## Summary table (Atlas only)

| Topic | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| **Step-by-step (one utterance)** | `route_semantic` → **one** tool → `execute_tool` → optional CSPE_TRANSPORT_RESULTS injection for **summarization**, not a second route with resolved ids. |
| **Where wrong args appear** | **`RouteDecision.args`** from the **router LLM** → passed through to `cspe_route` unchanged by orchestrator (no transport enricher). |
| **Issue locus** | **Routing / tool-arg generation** (single-shot `cspe_route` with human-readable strings in id fields). **Result handoff** does not preserve structured `station_id` for the next route. |

**Nothing in this trace contradicts** runtime evidence that canonical ids work when passed and names fail: Atlas often never supplies canonical ids because nothing in this pipeline **requires** or **stores** them for `cspe_route`.
